title: POV: YOU Owe $14,000 and Are Debt Free in 29 Months — Jake Is Still Paying for 7 Years

thumbnail.img: {HERO} standing calmly in the foreground smiling and holding a credit card cut in half, behind him a young man in a blue shirt panicking buried in a pile of bills and a snowy mountain with a rolling avalanche, strong contrast between calm and panic, composition with the hero on the left third

lines: It's a Sunday night. You spread every bill you owe across the kitchen table.
And for the first time, you add it all up.
scenes.img: {HERO} at a kitchen table at night with bills and envelopes spread out in front of him, a calculator and a cup of tea, serious but calm face, warm lamp light

lines: Fourteen thousand dollars.
Your stomach drops. Just for a second.
scenes.img: close-up of {HERO} staring at a calculator, eyebrows raised, a small bead of sweat, bills around him

lines: A twelve hundred dollar medical bill.
A five thousand five hundred dollar car loan at seven percent.
scenes.img: {HERO} holding up a hospital bill in one hand and a car key in the other, thoughtful face, kitchen at night

lines: And a credit card with seven thousand three hundred dollars on it.
At twenty five percent interest.
scenes.img: {HERO} holding a single credit card between two fingers looking at it with a worried frown, a glowing red warning symbol floating beside it

lines: Your friend Jake has almost the same pile.
His plan? Pay the minimums and hope.
scenes.img: a young man in a blue shirt on a messy couch shrugging and tossing bills into a drawer, carefree but tired face, cluttered living room

lines: Your friend Mia just texted you.
I'm doing the snowball method. Want to join?
scenes.img: a young woman with a ponytail smiling and typing on her phone on a bus, determined hopeful face, city outside the window

lines: So tonight, you do something different.
You run the numbers on all three plans. Jake's. Mia's. And one more.
scenes.img: {HERO} opening a laptop at the kitchen table, sleeves pushed up, focused calm expression, three paper stacks next to him

lines: Plan one. Jake's plan. Minimums only.
That's four hundred thirty dollars a month.
scenes.img: a young man in a blue shirt paying bills on his phone with a bored face, a calendar on the wall behind him

lines: The medical bill? Gone in two years.
The car loan? About two and a half.
scenes.img: a young man in a blue shirt looking at a wall calendar with months crossed off, slightly relieved

lines: But that credit card?
At one hundred eighty a month, it takes over seven years.
scenes.img: a young man in a blue shirt slowly aging on a couch, calendar pages flying through the air around him, credit card on the table

lines: Because every month, about one hundred fifty dollars of his payment is just interest.
He pays, and the balance barely moves.
scenes.img: a young man in a blue shirt pouring coins into a leaky bucket, the coins dripping out of a hole at the bottom, frustrated face

lines: Total interest on Jake's plan?
Almost nine thousand five hundred dollars.
scenes.img: a young man in a blue shirt staring in shock at a very long receipt unrolling across the floor of his living room

lines: Nine thousand five hundred dollars. For nothing.
That's a used car. Or a full emergency fund.
scenes.img: {HERO} at the kitchen table shaking his head slowly, a thought bubble showing a small used car and a piggy bank

lines: So before any method, you need one thing.
A little extra every month.
scenes.img: {HERO} leaning back in his chair at the kitchen table, thinking with one hand on his chin, notebook open

lines: You cancel two streaming services you barely watch.
That's thirty dollars.
scenes.img: {HERO} on a couch canceling a subscription on a tablet, a calm small smile

lines: You cook three more dinners at home each week instead of ordering in.
That's about one hundred dollars a month.
scenes.img: {HERO} cooking a simple pasta dinner in a small cozy kitchen, steam rising, happy relaxed face

lines: And you sell the bike you haven't ridden in a year, then call your phone company for a cheaper plan.
Another forty a month.
scenes.img: {HERO} on the phone in his living room smiling, a bicycle with a sold tag by the door

lines: One hundred seventy dollars extra.
Now you can pay six hundred a month instead of four thirty.
scenes.img: {HERO} writing $600 in a notebook with a confident smile, a jar of coins beside him

lines: Plan two. Mia's plan. The debt snowball.
Pay the minimums on everything. Then throw all the extra at the smallest balance.
scenes.img: a young woman with a ponytail rolling a small snowball down a snowy hill, cheerful determined face

lines: For Mia, that's the twelve hundred dollar medical bill.
And six months later, it's gone.
scenes.img: a young woman with a ponytail tearing a paid bill in half with a huge smile, confetti in her apartment

lines: That first win feels amazing.
Now that whole payment rolls onto the car loan.
scenes.img: a young woman with a ponytail with a growing snowball rolling behind her down a hill, excited face

lines: The car is paid off in month seventeen.
Then everything rolls onto the credit card.
scenes.img: a young woman with a ponytail holding car keys up proudly in front of her car, sunny parking lot

lines: Thirty months. Completely debt free.
About three thousand eight hundred dollars in interest.
scenes.img: a young woman with a ponytail jumping for joy in a park with a giant snowball behind her, sunny day

lines: Plan three. The one you keep looking at.
The debt avalanche.
scenes.img: {HERO} at his laptop looking at a mountain illustration on the screen, curious focused face

lines: Same minimums. Same six hundred dollars.
But the extra goes to the highest interest rate first. Not the smallest balance.
scenes.img: {HERO} pointing at a credit card pinned on a corkboard among other bills, calm determined expression

lines: For you, that's the credit card. Twenty five percent.
It's the debt that grows the fastest.
scenes.img: {HERO} standing in front of a big credit card shaped boulder at the top of a snowy mountain, ready to push it

lines: The hard part? For almost two years, no debt disappears.
You just watch the card balance shrink. Month after month.
scenes.img: {HERO} on a couch at night checking a slowly falling chart on his phone, patient calm face, rain on the window

lines: Jake asks why you're bothering.
You just smile. Every dollar you save on interest is a dollar that works for you.
scenes.img: a young man in a blue shirt laughing and pointing at {HERO} in a coffee shop, {HERO} smiling calmly with a cup of coffee

lines: Month twenty eight. The credit card hits zero.
The big one. The scary one. Gone.
scenes.img: {HERO} cutting a credit card in half at the kitchen table with a big relieved smile, morning sunlight

lines: One month later, the rest is gone too.
Twenty nine months. Debt free.
scenes.img: {HERO} standing on top of a snowy mountain with arms raised at sunrise, triumphant peaceful face

lines: So who won?
Here are the real numbers. Side by side.
scenes.img: {HERO} and a young woman with a ponytail sitting at a cafe table comparing notebooks, friendly curious mood

lines: Jake's minimums: about seven and a half years.
Nine thousand five hundred dollars in interest.
scenes.img: a young man in a blue shirt sitting alone surrounded by tall piles of bills, exhausted face

lines: Mia's snowball: thirty months.
Three thousand eight hundred in interest.
scenes.img: a young woman with a ponytail smiling holding a snowball, a little proud

lines: Your avalanche: twenty nine months.
About two thousand nine hundred in interest.
scenes.img: {HERO} smiling calmly holding a small mountain shaped trophy

lines: The avalanche saved you about nine hundred dollars more than the snowball.
And it finished one month sooner.
scenes.img: {HERO} putting a stack of bills into a piggy bank, satisfied smile

lines: But here's the part nobody tells you.
The difference between the two methods is small. The difference from Jake is huge.
scenes.img: {HERO} and a young woman with a ponytail high-fiving in a park, a young man in a blue shirt in the background looking at his phone

lines: The snowball gives you quick wins.
Research suggests those small wins help people stick with the plan.
scenes.img: a young woman with a ponytail checking off a list on her fridge with a marker, happy face

lines: The avalanche costs less.
But only if you don't quit in the long middle.
scenes.img: {HERO} jogging steadily up a long mountain path, calm focused face

lines: So pick the one you'll actually finish.
Need motivation? Snowball. Love the math? Avalanche.
scenes.img: {HERO} standing at a fork in a snowy mountain trail, one path with a small snowball sign and one with a mountain sign, thoughtful smile

lines: Either way, the real secret is the same.
Find extra money, and never stop at the minimum.
scenes.img: {HERO} setting up an automatic payment on his phone, a calm confident smile, cozy living room

lines: Twenty nine months later, it's Sunday night again.
The kitchen table is empty. No bills. Just a cup of tea.
scenes.img: {HERO} at a clean empty kitchen table at night with only a cup of tea, peaceful content smile, warm lamp light

lines: And that six hundred dollars a month?
Now it goes straight into your savings.
scenes.img: {HERO} watching a savings account grow on his phone, a glowing green chart beside him

lines: If this helped, subscribe for a new simple money move every day.
And tell me in the comments. Are you team snowball or team avalanche?
scenes.img: {HERO} waving warmly at the viewer in a cozy living room, friendly smile, warm light
